item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 💭 Perspective
💡 This perspective reframes creep in solid-state batteries from a narrow liability or benefit into a unified chemo-mechanical design parameter. It links classical creep loading to stack pressure, explains creep's intrinsic dual roles at interfaces, and proposes timescale-based design principles plus time-resolved operando characterization to rationally optimize creep, guiding durable next-generation alkali-metal solid-state battery design.

item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Cyanuric chloride is introduced as a concentration-tunable additive for Li-S batteries, with 0.05 M optimal. It enhances anion participation in Li-ion solvation, suppresses polysulfide crossover, and forms dual inorganic-rich interphases at cathode and anode. This yields 3000-cycle stability, 560 mAh g⁻¹ at 10C, and 72.73% pouch-cell retention, while showing that excess additive (0.10 M) degrades performance—highlighting concentration-dependent design.
